brief: Deutsche Bank's Henry Allen argues rates markets underprice inflation: either inflation rolls over or rates rise further, forcing risk assets to adjust. Fed hike pricing looks shallow despite hawkish Fed surprises in 4 of 5 years; August's ISM services prices-paid index hit a four-year high, pointing to CPI above 5 percent, while Warsh called the 2 percent target firm and fixed and strong payrolls free the Fed to focus on inflation. Since 4-5 percent inflation has historically brought over 200bp of first-year tightening, and one-and-done cycles are rare, implying a longer cycle than priced. ECB hike pricing has barely moved despite a jump in European gas and higher growth and inflation expectations, leaving euro vol subdued. Oil curve still prices a Strait of Hormuz reopening repeatedly pushed back; a persistent blockage would push the back end higher, removing support for equities and credit. Risk assets have shrugged off a sharp rise in real yields on resilient growth, but the next inflation shock looks like a negative supply shock, with policy cushions limited: inflation restricts rate cuts and high debt constrains fiscal stimulus. Volatility has collapsed even as rates and inflation risks build, just as VIX seasonality low point nears.
